newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: China gives lawnmowers to fight Colombia drug war.
newsitem.headline: China gives lawnmowers to fight Colombia drug war.

text.p: China struck an unusual blow in the international drug war on Wednesday by donating 19 gasoline-powered lawnmowers to this indigenous community nestled high in the Colombian Andes.
"These gifts, while small, are symbolic of Chinese support for the international war on drugs," Chinese Ambassador Huang Shikang told a 2,000-strong group of Guambiano Indians.
The Guambiano traditionally grow potatoes, beans, garlic and yucca on the steep slopes that tower above this mountain village at 10,500 feet (3,200 metres).
In the last five years they turned to growing opium poppies but decided to eradicate the illicit plantations of what they call the "cursed flower" after it began to cause rifts in the community.

Shikang donated the lawnmowers at a ceremony attended by President Ernesto Samper to mark the end of poppy cultivation in Silvia. The Chinese ambassador also handed over 45 industrial sewing machines and 19 electric generators as part of a $129,000 package of equipment that included two trucks.
Looking at the fleet of lawnmowers, one Guambiano dressed in his traditional purple and blue robes was grateful but confused.

"I'm not sure what we will do with them but I'm sure we will find a use," he said, suggesting that what little grass the local goats did not chew could be turned into mulch to fertilise the potato crop.
